cases.question: Under the NYC Fire Code, can a technician verify the sensitivity of a smoke detector in a building fire alarm system just by spraying an unmeasured aerosol concentration into it?
cases.expectedAnswer: No. Sensitivity must not be tested/measured with a device administering an unmeasured concentration of smoke or aerosol. A calibrated or otherwise specified method is needed.
cases.answerText: No. Under the 2022 NYC Fire Code, a smoke detector’s sensitivity must be checked using one of the specified calibrated methods or equipment (FC § 907.20.4), and “smoke detector sensitivity shall not be tested or measured using a device that administers an unmeasured concentration of smoke or other aerosol into the detector” (FC § 907.20.4.1). Spraying an unmeasured aerosol concentration into the detector therefore cannot serve as the sensitivity test. The separate exception for single-station smoke alarms does not apply to a detector connected to a building fire alarm system.

cases.operativeRuleReview: FC 907.20.4.1 prohibits unmeasured smoke/aerosol concentration for sensitivity testing;907.20.4 provides permitted calibrated/control-equipment methods and the single-station exception. All are present in cited text and accurately explained.

cases.applicabilityReview: The question specifies a detector connected to a building alarm system, so the single-station exception is correctly excluded.

cases.question: If a calibrated test shows that detector is outside its listed and marked sensitivity range, can we leave it as-is because it still triggers the alarm?
cases.expectedAnswer: No. A detector found outside its listed/marked range must be cleaned and recalibrated or replaced; the field-adjustable exception permits appropriate adjustment plus cleaning/recalibration or replacement. Alarm activation alone does not meet sensitivity compliance.
cases.answerText: **No.** FC § 907.20.4 requires a smoke detector found outside its listed and marked sensitivity range to be cleaned and recalibrated or replaced; the fact that it still triggers an alarm does not satisfy that requirement (2022 NYC FC § 907.20.4). The field-adjustable exception permits adjustment within the listed and marked range, plus cleaning and recalibration, or replacement—it does not permit leaving an out-of-range detector as-is. The stated exception for single-station smoke alarms does not apply to detectors in a building fire alarm system.
